problems.title: Invalid minimum-distance inference
problems.source_claim: Lemma 3.4 equation (3.18) and equation (3.44), used in (3.45)-(3.46)
problems.assumptions: Original H1-H4, noncollision bootstrap dmin>=8R; distinguish scalar diagnostic from particle hypotheses.
problems.check: Duhamel yields fixed-pair distance integral. Minimization at final time cannot replace larger historical pair distance by dmin inside negative integral. y=2-t^2 on [0,7/5] is positive decreasing and satisfies y>=y(0)/2-integral y, yet y(7/5)=1/25<exp(-7/5). y_epsilon=2-(2-epsilon)t^2 on [0,1] yields no positive uniform terminal bound.
problems.result: The displayed implication is invalid; not a particle counterexample or proof that Theorem 1.1 is false.
problems.counterevidence: Full damped relative ODE contains additional structure; a cone comparison works given uniform L<=6*pi*gamma*lambda/4, not established by H4 and displayed initial-layer estimates.
problems.impact: Core dependency: minimum-distance estimate closes main Theorem 1.1 bootstrap on p30. Appendix B repeats it for Theorem 2.3.

correction.statement: With |b|<=L|r| and L<=a/4, D+z<=z^2-a*z+a*L and z(0)<=a/2 imply |r(t)|>=|r(0)| exp[-2z(0)/a-2Lt]. Binary intended-range bootstrap supplies uniform L for large lambda; Stokes H1-H4 repair remains unverified.

problems.title: False growing-kernel domain of Theorems 2.1 and 2.3
problems.source_claim: For alpha<d-1 and prescribed initial Wp/separation smallness, Wp remains bounded by C exp(Ct) times initial distance plus inverse inertia.

assumptions.particle_data: midpoint n^3 grid with one y coordinate moved to L=N^(3/4)

problems.check: Kernel smooth, div=0, |K|+|x||grad K|<=3|x|^2; global volume-preserving continuum shear has L2 norm1. Initial W1<=sqrt(3)/(2n)+(L-y0)/N ->0; dmin=N^-1/3; smallness exponent4/5, factors2 (Thm2.1) and1/2 (Thm2.3). Transverse coordinates fixed, same transverse points have equal x speed, so no collisions. Empirical x-mean velocity 2(s_N-m_N^2), continuum1/6. Difference asymptotic2N^1/2. D2,D3 trivial for zero V0; second-order displacement factor t-(1-e^-Nt)/N. Complete allN construction given in report.
problems.result: For fixed t>0, W1>=2tN^1/2(1+o(1)) while claimed upper bound tends to0.
problems.counterevidence: The physical Oseen kernel alpha=1 is excluded from this counterexample. Imposing nonnegative alpha excludes mechanism but changes stated domain.
problems.impact: False independent general-kernel guarantees; not a refutation of physical sedimentation theorem.

correction.statement: For example impose 0<=alpha<d-1; this excludes example and matches positive-beta lemma application, but full revised theorem not certified.

problems.title: Auxiliary Stokes fields violate boundary or PDE conditions
problems.source_claim: Piecewise Stokeslet with minus Laplacian correction represents surface force; displayed curl velocity and pressure solve exterior Stokes equation.
problems.assumptions: R,r>0; G=W=e1; trace at Re1 and exterior point2re1; standard positive Laplacian convention fixed by -Delta u+grad p.
problems.check: Minus field trace=e1/(3piR), interior=e1/(6piR). Plus sign matches trace and equation3.6. For pressure r grad(1/|x|).W, residual at2re1=5e1/(8r^2); corrected pressure=3r(W.x)/(2|x|^3) yields zero symbolic residual.
problems.result: Actual boundary jump and nonzero PDE residual; not merely constant pressure gauge.
problems.counterevidence: Correct weak solutions independently defined; Section3 uses plus sign; decay/scaling estimates unchanged by verified field corrections.
problems.impact: Local construction must be corrected; no additional failure of resistance theorem established.

correction.statement: Replace minus Laplacian correction by plus; replace pressure by -(3r/2)grad(1/|x|).W throughout cutoff and weight. Choose cutoff1 on B_(d/2).

checks.disposition: supported with the report's proof-gap boundary
checks.reason: The fixed-pair Duhamel estimate gives d_ij(t)>=d_ij(0)/2-C integral d_ij(s)A(s) ds. Selecting a pair minimizing at t does not allow replacement of its earlier, possibly larger distances by d_min(s) inside the negative integral. Independently, a lower integral inequality does not have the asserted lower-Gronwall consequence: y=2-t^2 stays positive on [0,7/5], and y+integral(y)-1=1+2t-t^2-t^3/3 is concave with positive endpoint values 1 and 347/375; nevertheless y(7/5)=1/25<exp(-7/5). The family 2-(2-epsilon)t^2 on [0,1] has the same fixed initial value and a positive inequality margin, but arbitrary positive terminal epsilon. Equation3.44 is used to close3.45-3.46, so this affects the main proof rather than an isolated presentation detail.
checks.counterevidence: These scalar functions are diagnostics of the inference, not particle solutions satisfying H1-H4. The full damped relative ODE contains information absent from the scalar inequality. No counterexample to the physical Theorem1.1 is established.
checks.repair_check: For r''+a r'=a b and |b|<=L|r|, z=|r'|/|r| satisfies D+z<=z^2-a z+a L. If L<=a/4 and z(0)<=a/2, the cone is invariant and z'<=-a z/2+a L, giving |r(t)|>=|r(0)|exp[-2z(0)/a-2Lt]. H3 gives the initial cone condition. H4 only bounds |V0|_infinity/lambda by an arbitrary fixed constant; the displayed initial-layer bound does not prove the required smallness for the Stokes system. A genuinely N-uniform binary Lipschitz coefficient permits the conditional repair for sufficiently large lambda, without repairing P2's global domain.

checks.disposition: supported exact theorem counterexample in the stated growing-kernel range
checks.reason: For d=3, alpha=-2, p=1, q=q'=2, the smooth kernel K(x)=(x_2^2,0,0) is divergence-free and obeys |K|+|x||grad K|<=3|x|^2, with q>3/4. Unit-cube density has the global volume-preserving shear x_1 -> x_1+t(x_2^2-x_2+1/3), preserving L2 norm1. On N=n^3 midpoint points, move one y0=1-1/(2n) to L=N^(3/4). Initial W1<=sqrt(3)/(2n)+(L-y0)/N tends to zero, while d_min=N^(-1/3). The exponent is4/5; the smallness multipliers are2 for equation2.3 and1/2 for D1, which must not be interchanged. The exact moments are m1=1/2+(L-y0)/N and m2=1/3-1/(12n^2)+(L^2-y0^2)/N. Particle barycentric x velocity is2(m2-m1^2), whereas the continuum value is1/6. Thus W1(t)>=t|2(m2-m1^2)-1/6|~2tN^(1/2). Transverse coordinates are fixed; particles with identical transverse coordinates have equal x velocity, so no collision invalidates the example. For Theorem2.3 choose zero initial velocity and lambda=N; D2-D3 hold, and the particle displacement uses t-(1-exp(-Nt))/N, giving the same divergence. The all-N extension by retaining N points from a ceil(N^(1/3))^3 grid changes initial transport by O(N^(-1/3)); grid spacing remains comparable and the cube subsequence already contradicts the conclusion.
checks.counterevidence: This example uses alpha=-2 and unbounded second moments in a vanishing outlier mass. Neither a nonnegative-alpha restriction nor a second-moment hypothesis occurs in the stated general theorem. It does not refute the physical Oseen alpha=1 theorem.
checks.repair_check: Restricting to0<=alpha<d-1 excludes this example and aligns positive beta with Lemma2.4, but excluding one counterexample is not a proof of the fully revised theorem.

checks.reason: For Phi=(I/|x|+xx^T/|x|^3)/(8*pi), Delta Phi=(I/|x|^3-3xx^T/|x|^5)/(4*pi). At x=R e1 with G=e1, the printed minus correction has exterior trace e1/(3*pi*R), twice the interior trace; it is not the required H1 field. The plus correction already present in3.6 gives the constant correct trace. The curl of the printed vector potential is (3r/(4s)+r^3/(4s^3))W+(3r/(4s^3)-3r^3/(4s^5))(W.x)x. The displayed pressure is -r(W.x)/s^3; at2r e1 with W=e1 its Stokes residual is5 e1/(8r^2), so the discrepancy is not a pressure gauge.
checks.counterevidence: The weak Stokes solutions are defined independently, and the correct plus formula is already available in Section3. These local mistakes alone do not disprove the resistance estimates or the physical limit.
checks.repair_check: Use the plus Laplacian correction and pressure3r(W.x)/(2s^3). These give zero exterior residual, boundary velocity W, and traction -sigma n=3W/(2r). Choosing the cutoff equal to1 on B_(d/2), not merely B_r, confines its derivatives to the specified annulus; d>=4r allows the stated derivative bounds. The reciprocal identity then supplies the force representation, normalized mean weight I, and the required scale bounds.
